notes: [{"version":"0.2.21","date":"2026-11-07","notes":["Shared hosts need the server from this release: upload the new server folder before updating RemoteX. Older RemoteX versions keep working against it.","Jump hosts for shared websites: a shared website can go \"Through host\" a shared SSH host of the same collection. A new setting on shared SSH hosts, \"Members can open SSH\", decides whether members may use the host itself. Turned off, members never see the host or its login. They only reach the website through it, and the tunnel goes to that website's address and port and nowhere else. Admins keep full access.","Share to on a website whose Through host is one of your own hosts offers to share both. The SSH host goes along with members locked out of it. Deleting or moving a jump host that a shared website still uses is refused, naming the websites.","A shared host's note now belongs to the team: it travels encrypted with the host, every member reads it and admins edit it. It can't point at a file in your notes folder. Share to copies the text of your own host's note into the shared host.","Members see less they can't use on a shared host: no empty edit bar, no tags (shared hosts never kept them), no Forget on the host key and no Toolbox.","A collection's Access tab has Save and Cancel. Ticking people no longer applies at once.","RemoteX checks every minute whether a collection changed on the server. A collection with changes waiting gets a refresh button at the right end of its row, and hovering the row lists what changed. Refresh applies that collection only; unlocking still applies everything, and a collection you were just given appears right away.","An admin who hasn't refreshed since another admin gave a collection a new key can no longer save hosts, rename it or hand out keys with the old one. RemoteX asks to refresh first, so members never receive a host or key they can't open.","Settings → About lists what's new in every version between yours and the update before you install it. This starts with the next update after this one."]},{"version":"0.2.20","date":"2026-11-07","notes":["Fixed: file dialogs RemoteX opens itself stayed shut while a website tab was open, so \"Save recovery key…\" in Settings → Shared hosts did nothing. The same went for other save and open dialogs and for the paste confirm in pop-out windows. They all open again."]},{"version":"0.2.19","date":"2026-11-07","notes":["New, opt-in: shared hosts. A small server your team runs (PHP with SQLite, in the server folder of the RemoteX repository) holds a catalog of hosts for everyone to connect to. RemoteX encrypts every host on your device before it leaves, so the server only stores ciphertext. Sign-in runs through Microsoft Entra ID. Without a catalog, RemoteX stays local and makes no calls to any server.","Server setup: upload the server and open /install on it. The page walks you through the Entra app registration with the server's own addresses, checks everything with a Microsoft sign-in, and shows the invite code. Whoever finishes it creates the catalog.","Joining: Settings → Shared hosts → Connect, paste the invite code and sign in. An admin approves your device after comparing four words with you, for example by phone. Your collections then show above your own hosts, each one collapsible.","Admins edit shared hosts in the usual host form and confirm each change before it reaches everyone. Right-click one of your own hosts → Share to copies it into a collection, with its password or SSH key; your own host stays as it is.","A collection's pane has Access (tick who gets it; removing someone gives the collection a new key and re-encrypts its hosts), Audit (who changed what, when) and Rotate key. Settings → Shared hosts lists devices waiting for approval, devices that need your check, and all devices with Revoke for a lost laptop. A dot on the gear shows when someone waits.","Your own state for shared hosts stays in your vault: last connected, history, pins and notes links. Offline, shared hosts are hidden until the next sync.","Under the hood: Tauri 2.12 and its updater 2.14, which drops a zip library version with a known crash bug."]},{"version":"0.2.18","date":"2026-11-01","notes":["New host type \"OpenCode (web)\": RemoteX starts opencode on the host over SSH and shows its web interface in a tab, the same way VS Code hosts work. Pick the project folder in the host's settings. The tab, Files, Browse, Key auth, tab restore and the Vaultwarden panel behave as on a VS Code host.","Use your own model: paste an opencode.json into the host's settings, for example a local OpenAI-compatible server with its address and model names. RemoteX hands it to opencode on every start without writing anything to the host, and a checkbox turns it off without deleting it. RemoteX also stops opencode from downloading its online model catalog.","If opencode isn't installed on the host, the tab offers \"install opencode\", which runs opencode's official install script into ~/.opencode/bin. Your shell config files are left alone.","The host's dot in the sidebar shows when opencode is working, and pops when it waits for you to allow a command or answer a question, like the Claude dot on VS Code hosts.","Toolbox docker-stats: s, t and r start, stop or restart the selected container after a [y/N] confirm. The list keeps updating while docker works, and the result or docker's error shows in the message line."]},{"version":"0.2.17","date":"2026-10-29","notes":["The Vaultwarden key button now shows on every connection tab, not only websites: SSH and local terminals, RDP, Files, VS Code and SQL Server. \"This host\" lists the logins with a URI whose address is the host's address (ssh://server, rdp://10.0.0.5 or just the name; the port doesn't matter). A local shell has no address, so its panel offers search only.","New \"Type\" button in SSH and local terminal tabs: it types the login's password into the terminal, for example at a sudo prompt, without pressing Enter. The password goes from RemoteX straight into the terminal and never through the clipboard. Logins with \"Master password re-prompt\" still ask first.","In a workspace, the notes and Vaultwarden buttons moved to the right end of the header, after the layout buttons, where they sit for a single host."]},{"version":"0.2.16","date":"2026-10-29","notes":["New: several Vaultwarden connections. Settings → Vaultwarden lists them, and \"Add connection\" adds another. The panel beside a website tab shows the logins of every unlocked connection in one list; a locked one sits as a row above the list and unlocks in place.","Organization logins: the panel now shows the logins of your Vaultwarden organizations too. A connection's personal vault and each organization get their own tab once there is more than one. In \"All\", each login shows its source's icon before the name and a faint glow in its colour, stronger on the selected row. Name, colour and icon (12 to choose from) are set per source in Settings.","Test login in Settings: with an API key it checks the connection without the master password and lists Personal and each organization with its number of logins. Tick the ones you want; unticked ones are never decrypted. An organization you join later stays off until you turn it on, and the panel says so.","\"Keep unlocked with RemoteX\" (connections with an API key): tick it when you unlock and the panel opens without the master password after every RemoteX unlock. RemoteX keeps your Vaultwarden account key in its encrypted vault for this; \"Forget stored key\" in Settings removes it. Items with \"Master password re-prompt\" still ask.","Logins in an organization collection that hides passwords can't have their password copied: the button is greyed out. Username and TOTP still copy."]},{"version":"0.2.15","date":"2026-10-29","notes":["New: host notes as Markdown files in a folder of your choice (Settings → Notes). Any folder works, including an mdkb vault, which picks up the changes RemoteX makes. Link a host to an existing note or create one; new notes go to <group>/<host>/<host>.md. Notes in the folder are plain files, not encrypted like the vault, and Settings says so.","Notes open in the same live-preview editor as mdkb and save on their own about a second after you stop typing. If another program changed the note in the meantime, RemoteX asks whether to reload theirs, overwrite with yours, or save yours as a copy. Notes locked in mdkb are read-only. Ctrl+click a [[link]] to follow it (Back returns), Ctrl+click a #tag to list the notes that carry it, and paste screenshots straight into a note.","Notes show in the host's Details, in their own tab, and in a panel on the right of any session tab or workspace: click the notes button at the right end of the tab bar or press Ctrl+Shift+N. In a workspace the panel lets you pick which host's notes to show. Drag the panel's left edge to resize it.","Notes you already had in RemoteX stay where they are until you choose a folder. Then they become read-only, and \"Move to notes folder\" in the host's Details turns them into a note file.","The Vaultwarden button moved from the website address bar to the right end of the tab bar, next to the notes button, and shares the same panel. Its width setting is gone: drag the panel edge instead.","The tab bar stays on one line: the host's Details and Notes tabs stay put at the left, and when the session tabs don't fit, ‹ › buttons slide them one tab at a time. The mouse wheel scrolls them too.","Security updates: Angular 20.3.34 and, in the RDP helper, libz-sys 1.1.31."]},{"version":"0.2.14","date":"2026-10-29","notes":["New (Windows): Vaultwarden logins next to website tabs. Set up the connection in Settings → Vaultwarden with your server address, email and either a personal API key or your master password with two-step login (authenticator app or email code). A key button then appears in every website tab's address bar and opens a panel beside the page. The page gets narrower but stays usable.","The panel lists the logins that match the current page first, then all your logins, with a search over names, usernames and addresses. Matching follows each item's URI match setting from Vaultwarden. Each row has buttons to copy the username, the password or the current TOTP code. Copies are kept out of Windows clipboard history (Win+V) and cloud clipboard. RemoteX only reads your vault: it never fills in pages and never changes items.","The master password is asked the first time you open the panel after unlocking RemoteX, and is never saved. RemoteX asks for it again only when the server ends the session, and forgets everything it decrypted when RemoteX locks. Items with \"Master password re-prompt\" ask for it before each password or TOTP copy. Archived items show up only when you search. Organization items are not shown yet.","The back, forward, reload and open-in-browser buttons of website tabs have a new look that matches the rest of RemoteX.","Fixed: closing RemoteX with a website tab open left the RemoteX process running in the background, so it could not be started again or updated until it was ended in Task Manager."]},{"version":"0.2.13","date":"2026-10-28","notes":["Each time you unlock the vault, RemoteX keeps a copy of it as it was before this session, named with the date and the RemoteX version, for example vault.enc.2026-10-28_101233.v0.2.13.bak. Nothing writes to these copies while RemoteX is open, so after an update you can still open the vault in the older version. The last 5 copies are kept, and unlocking without any changes since the last copy adds none. To go back to one, rename it to the vault's file name. If the copy cannot be written, the vault still opens and RemoteX tells you so."]},{"version":"0.2.12","date":"2026-10-28","notes":["Microsoft Defender quarantined RemoteX 0.2.10 and 0.2.11 as \"Trojan:Win32/Bearfoos.A!ml\". This was a false alarm from its automatic analysis, most likely triggered by website tabs saving their login cookies into the vault. That feature is removed: logins that a site keeps only until the browser closes, such as OPNsense's, now end when RemoteX closes or locks, like in a normal browser. Logins with an expiry date still persist. Cookies saved by 0.2.10 or 0.2.11 are deleted from the vault the next time you unlock it."]},{"version":"0.2.11","date":"2026-10-28","notes":["A website host's \"Through host\" field lists every SSH host with its full folder path, such as Infra / Proxmox / pve-2. Type part of a name, folder or address to narrow the list. If the host it pointed to was deleted, the field says so and you have to pick another one, or Direct, before saving.","Dropdowns have a new look throughout the app, in RemoteX's own colours instead of the system list. Lists that grow with your data can be searched by typing: Group and group Parent (with the folder path, so two \"New group\"s are no longer confused), Use a stored key (name or fingerprint), MSSQL databases (host form and workbench) and MSSQL logins. Short fixed lists such as Theme or Protocol still jump to an entry when you press its first letter.","Text fields look the same everywhere. On Settings → Programs, the browser path fields were drawn in the default system style and too narrow to read; they now match the Open with rows. Fields on the unlock screen and in dialogs are a little smaller, the new-tag field in host Details a little larger.","Settings → Tags lines up: colours come first, then the name, a preview of the tag and the delete button, in the same columns on every row. Drag a tag by the ⠿ handle or by its preview to reorder."]},{"version":"0.2.10","date":"2026-10-28","notes":["New (Windows): website hosts. Pick \"Website\" as a host's protocol and give it a URL. Connect opens the site in a RemoteX tab, which also works in workspaces and pop-out windows. Each website host has its own browser profile, so logins stay apart per host and persist across restarts. Deleting the host deletes its profile.","A website tab has back, forward and reload buttons and an address field. Type an address and press Enter to go there (https:// is added when missing); Esc puts the current address back. Back and forward are greyed out when there is no page that way. The ↗ button opens the current page in your normal browser.","Through host: a website host can go out through one of your SSH hosts, so the page and its DNS lookups leave from that machine. It uses the same tunnel as Browse, with nothing installed on the SSH host. Changing the setting reloads the host's open tabs on the new route.","Logins that a site keeps only until the browser closes, such as OPNsense's, are stored in the vault when the tab closes, on Lock and on quit, and are restored the next time you open the site. Login cookies shared across a whole domain (single sign-on) are kept too.","Self-signed certificates, common on Proxmox, NAS and router pages, prompt once, like RDP. Once you trust the fingerprint, the site loads without asking again. If the certificate later changes, RemoteX refuses it until you remove the old one. Trusted certificates are listed in the host's Details, each with a remove button.","Shortcuts in a website tab: Ctrl+T opens another tab of the site, Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the last closed website tab at the page it was on, Ctrl+R reloads, and Ctrl+Shift+R reloads without the cache.","Links that open a new window open as a new tab of the same host, next to the current one. A page can open at most three this way within ten seconds; the tab says when it blocked more. A website host set to single instance has one tab: Connect switches to it, and the + button is hidden.","While a menu, dialog, host card or Settings covers a website, the page underneath shows as a dimmed still picture and returns to live when the overlay closes.","With Settings → Sessions → Restore sessions on, website tabs come back at the page they were on."]},{"version":"0.2.9","date":"2026-10-26","notes":["0.2.8 was never released (its security check failed on newly published advisories). Its changes listed below ship in this version.","Security: updated the big-integer arithmetic under the SSH and RDP crypto (crypto-bigint 0.7.10, ctutils 0.4.6), where some operations meant to run in constant time could branch on secret values (RUSTSEC-2026-0387). No visible changes.","Internal: a build tool dependency was updated for a denial-of-service advisory (undici 6.29.1, under the Angular CLI)."]},{"version":"0.2.8","date":"2026-10-26","notes":["New: open a whole workspace in its own window. Right-click its row → Open in new window, or click the ⧉ next to its name. Every tab moves over live: terminals keep their history, MSSQL its query and results, SFTP its folder, RDP its desktop. Only a VS Code tab reloads its page and reconnects. The window works like the workspace view (layout, rename, splitters, Broadcast, Stop / Start, tab menus), and closing it brings the workspace back. Several workspaces can be out at once.","A terminal opened in its own window (\"Open in new window\") now keeps the colours of its earlier output. Everything else about it works as before.","The Stop / Start icons on a hovered workspace row in the sidebar are gone: they were too easy to click by accident. Stop and Start stay in the workspace header, its right-click menu and its hover card."]},{"version":"0.2.7","date":"2026-10-23","notes":["0.2.6 was never released (its security check failed on newly published advisories). Its changes listed below ship in this version.","Security: updated the certificate checks used for update downloads (rustls-webpki 0.103.16, webpki-root-certs 1.0.11), which no longer trust the distrusted emSign intermediates (RUSTSEC-2026-0382, 0383). Also updated the constant-time helpers under the SSH crypto (ctutils 0.4.5, RUSTSEC-2026-0385) in the app and the RDP helper, and tokio (1.54.1, RUSTSEC-2026-0386). No visible changes.","Internal: build tool dependencies updated for four advisories in the build toolchain (vite, the MCP SDK under the Angular CLI, body-parser). A yanked clipboard library version was replaced (clipboard-win 5.4.3)."]},{"version":"0.2.6","date":"2026-10-23","notes":["Closing RemoteX while sessions are connected or connecting now asks first, so a stray click on the window's close button no longer ends them all.","Fixed: when two RDP hosts with untrusted certificates connected at the same time, the second certificate prompt replaced the first and that tab stayed on \"connecting\". The prompts now come one after the other.","The tag filter in the sidebar has its own \"Tags\" header, like Pinned and Workspaces, with Clear at the right end of it."]},{"version":"0.2.5","date":"2026-10-20","notes":["Closing a tab inside a workspace (its × or a middle-click) now sends it back to its host, still connected, instead of ending the session. The tab menu in a workspace no longer has Close; close the tab from its host.","Workspace rows in the sidebar show Claude activity from their VS Code tabs, like host rows: a blue pulsing dot while Claude works, and an orange flash and dot when it waits for you.","Fixed: in a narrow sidebar, the Stop / Start icons on a hovered workspace row were pushed out of view. They now sit over the end of the name."]},{"version":"0.2.4","date":"2026-10-20","notes":["New: right-click a tab in a workspace → Go to host. It opens the host the tab belongs to, expands its groups and scrolls it into view in the sidebar, without moving the tab. The host shows the tab as its usual chip, whose \"Go to workspace\" takes you back.","The tab menu item that moves a tab out of its workspace is renamed from \"Back to host\" to \"Move back to host\". Going from a key's \"Used by\" list to a host now also scrolls the host into view."]},{"version":"0.2.3","date":"2026-10-19","notes":["Fixed: on Windows, local shells reconnected after restarting RemoteX could show as connected but stay blank, with no prompt and no startup command. They now start normally.","Fixed: in a narrow window the Stop / Start buttons in the workspace header slid under Broadcast. The header now moves its right-hand buttons to a second line when space runs out.","Fixed: the hover icons on a stopped workspace row sat further right than on a running one."]},{"version":"0.2.2","date":"2026-10-18","notes":["New: Start / Stop, opt-in under Settings → Features. Stop disconnects a session and keeps its tab where it is, so a workspace keeps its layout and the terminal keeps its scrollback; Start reconnects it in the same tab. Each tab has a small stop or start icon next to its ×, the tab menu has Stop and Start, and the hover cards list sessions with their own buttons.","A whole workspace can be stopped and started too: buttons in the middle of the workspace header, icons on its sidebar row, and entries in its right-click menu. Stop asks first, because programs running in those sessions end. It is unavailable while the workspace has an MSSQL tab or a running Toolbox task, and Start never re-runs a task.","Stopped tabs stay stopped after lock and restart, and no longer connect on their own when you open them.","Workspace rows in the sidebar show how many tabs are connected, for example \"4/6\", in green when all of them are. A workspace with nothing connected is dimmed with its name in italics.","The host hover card lists the host's open sessions, including the ones that live in a workspace.","Fixed: a hover card could disappear when the mouse moved slowly from the sidebar into it. The card also sits a little closer to the sidebar."]},{"version":"0.2.1","date":"2026-10-18","notes":["New: workspaces. A Workspaces section in the sidebar (between Pinned and your hosts) holds named split views with up to four panes, each with its own tabs, from any host. Right-click a session tab → Send to workspace, or a host → Open new session in workspace. Inside a workspace you drag tabs between panes, drag the dividers (each one on its own), pick one of six layouts in the header bar, and rename the workspace there too. Host views work exactly as before: a tab you sent away shows as a dim chip with \"Go to workspace\" and \"Move back here\". Workspaces are on by default; Settings → Features turns them off (their tabs go back to their hosts).","The two 2x2 layouts grow: drag a tab and a \"+\" appears at the end of each row and below the last one, up to 5 rows of 5 panes. \"2x2 columns\" does the same with columns. Panes that lose their last tab close up on their own.","Workspaces and the tabs inside them come back after lock and restart, in the same panes. An option under Settings → Features → Workspaces decides whether \"Send to workspace\" takes you there or keeps you on the host.","New: broadcast input inside a workspace, opt-in under Settings → Features → Workspaces. Once enabled, \"Broadcast\" in the workspace header (or Ctrl+Shift+B) lets you tick SSH and local terminals; what you type in one ticked terminal goes to all of them. Receiving panes get an orange frame, pastes always ask \"Paste into N terminals?\" first, and leaving the workspace switches it off.","New: paste guard. Pasting more than one line into a terminal asks first and shows what you are about to paste, since each line can run as a command. Turn it off in Settings → Sessions.","Tags can be reordered by dragging: a host's or group's tags in its details, and the global order in Settings → Tags.","The host hover card has an edit button that opens the host's details for editing.","Settings is reorganised into seven tabs and opens on Features: Features (workspaces with their options underneath, Keys list), Sessions (restore sessions plus the terminal settings), Appearance, Programs (Open with, browsers for Browse through host, sqlpackage), Tags, Vault and About.","Fixed: reordering a VS Code tab reloaded it. Fixed: with several terminals on screen, text in some of them could turn into garbled or missing characters."]},{"version":"0.2.0","date":"2026-10-18","notes":["SSH keys now live in one list in the vault. Turn on Settings → Features → \"Keys list\" to get a Hosts / Keys switch at the top of the sidebar: every key with the hosts that use it, plus its details and history (created, assigned, installed, rotated, exported, renamed, host deleted). You can rename, export and import keys there, and a key a host still uses can't be deleted. The switch is off by default and only hides the list; keys work the same either way.","Hosts can share a key. A host's Key auth section has \"Use stored key…\" to pick one from the list, and \"Remove from host\" replaces \"Delete key\": the host lets go of the key and the key stays in the list. Deleting a host keeps its key, duplicating a host shares the key, and rotating a key that other hosts also use only moves this host to the new key.","The SSH keys tool can store a generated key in the vault, save it to a file, or both. The passphrase only protects the file copy. Settings → Vault sets which boxes are ticked by default.","VS Code hosts now have a Key auth section, like SSH hosts.","The vault file format changes to version 2. On the first unlock RemoteX asks before upgrading and saves a copy of the old file next to it (for example vault.enc.v1.bak). Older RemoteX versions can't open the upgraded vault, only that copy.","New Settings → Sessions: \"Restore sessions\" reconnects the tabs that were connected when RemoteX locked or closed, and reopens the tab that was active. It is on by default. Turn it off to get the old behaviour, where restored tabs connect only when you open them."]},{"version":"0.1.70","date":"2026-10-18","notes":["0.1.69 was never released (its security check failed on newly published advisories). Its hosts sidebar changes listed below ship in this version.","Security: updated the TLS library (rustls 0.23.46) in the app and the RDP helper. Fixes TLS secrets showing up in debug output, a downgrade of later connections to classical key exchange, a large memory allocation before the server is authenticated, and data sent to the wrong server after an ECH rejection (RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to 0349). No visible changes.","Internal: build tools updated (Angular CLI 20.3.40 and its dependencies) for two advisories in the build toolchain. The zip advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0367 to 0369 in the updater are reviewed and accepted: RemoteX only unpacks updates whose signature it has already checked, and it ships an installer, not a zip."]},{"version":"0.1.69","date":"2026-10-18","notes":["Hosts sidebar: hovering a host opens a card with its full address (with a copy button), all tags, protocol, group path, auth, open sessions, detected OS, VS Code target or MSSQL database, last connection and the first line of its notes. You can move the mouse into the card. The address no longer takes up space in the row itself.","Hosts sidebar: when the panel is too narrow, tags shrink to dots in their colour instead of being cut off, starting from the rightmost. The host name always stays readable, and hovering a dot shows its tag name. Group rows whose tags shrank get a card too.","Hosts sidebar: selecting tags in the tag filter no longer hides the Pinned section.","Hosts sidebar: \"+ group\" and \"+ host\" now create inside the selected group, or next to the selected host. With nothing selected they still create at the top level."]},{"version":"0.1.68","date":"2026-10-05","notes":["Security: a VS Code tab now only answers requests that come from RemoteX itself. Before, a website open in your normal browser could reach the VS Code server through its local port while the tab was open. The VS Code frame is also sandboxed, so a page inside it can no longer replace the RemoteX window.","Locking the vault now closes every live connection, including Browse tunnels and connections that were still being set up when you locked.","SSH: pasting a large amount of text while the server was printing a lot of output could freeze the terminal for good, and closing the tab didn't free it. Fixed. A host that suddenly offers a different key type than the one you trusted now shows the \"host key changed\" warning instead of the \"new host\" prompt.","Detached terminal windows now keep up with heavy output instead of dropping text.","MSSQL: negative decimal and money values display correctly (they showed as e.g. -1.-50, also in copies and CSV exports), datetimeoffset values keep their offset, and datetime values round the way SSMS shows them.","MSSQL Edit Top 200: switching the database or running different SQL turns the grid read-only, so Save can no longer write to the table in the database the tab was opened on. Select Top 1000 and Edit Top 200 always run in their own tab, never in the tab you clicked while they connected. Ctrl+Z right after switching tabs no longer brings back the other tab's query. Editing rows of tables without a primary key now works with date, binary and negative decimal columns.","MSSQL: very large results are capped (32 MB total, 64 KB per cell) instead of crashing the app, a dropped connection reconnects on the next run, an error in the middle of a script keeps the results before it, Export CSV exports exactly what the grid shows, and saved queries are no longer lost when you lock while they are being restored.","BACPAC export and import no longer pass the SQL password on the sqlpackage command line, where other programs and process logs could see it.","Files: overwriting a file no longer deletes the original before the new copy is in place, and a failed overwrite keeps the new copy and names it in the error. Renaming in the local pane refuses to replace an existing file. Two tabs downloading the same file into the same folder no longer mix their contents. Uploading a file onto a remote folder of the same name is refused. On Linux, downloads and folder uploads land in the right folder again. On Windows, downloaded files are marked as coming from another computer. Names with hidden text-direction characters are rejected, and Cancel shows \"Cancelled\" instead of an error.","Vault: if saving a new master password fails, the old password stays in effect. Moving the vault refuses to overwrite another vault. A duplicated host uses its own copy of the key. Typing a password on a key-auth host no longer switches it to password login. Settings written by a newer RemoteX survive being saved by an older one, and crafted key or vault files can no longer freeze the app.","Several new-host key prompts now queue instead of replacing each other, locking clears passwords you were still typing, note links containing underscores open the right address, deleting a host from the sidebar keeps the host you are viewing, and MSSQL hosts show \"MSSQL\" as their protocol.","Native RDP (mstsc): the password RemoteX hands to Windows is now kept only until you sign out of Windows, even if RemoteX crashes before removing it.","Updates: installing an update with sessions open asks first and shuts VS Code servers down cleanly, and an update that would install an older version is refused.","Internal: the release build now uses pinned, checksummed build tools and actions and signs the installer in a separate step; build dependencies updated."]},{"version":"0.1.67","date":"2026-10-05","notes":["Security: updated the TLS library (rustls 0.23.45) in the app and the RDP helper, fixing a flaw where a TLS 1.3 connection could accept handshake messages at the wrong stage (RUSTSEC-2026-0285). The RDP helper also gets cryptoki 0.12.1, which fixes an out-of-bounds read when reading smart-card key attributes (RUSTSEC-2026-0286). No visible changes."]},{"version":"0.1.66","date":"2026-10-05","notes":["VS Code tabs no longer ask whether you trust the folder the first time you open them, and never fall back to Restricted Mode with extensions switched off. RemoteX now opens every VS Code folder and workspace as trusted. Workspace Trust is the VS Code feature that stops a folder from running its own tasks or debug configurations before you have agreed to it, so this is now off for every RemoteX VS Code tab.","Editing a VS Code host whose target is a raw workspace JSON no longer turns it into a Folder host when you save. The edit form used to show such a host as a Folder host, and saving kept that."]},{"version":"0.1.65","date":"2026-09-03","notes":["VS Code tabs open again on hosts running VS Code 1.136 or newer. That version started serving the workbench with headers that tell a browser to refuse being embedded in another page, so the tab showed \"127.0.0.1 refused to connect\" while the server was perfectly healthy and the same address still opened in a normal browser.
